rfm_tuples.R: Implied: insider transactions of the CEO, CFO, and Board of Directors are consistent with management commitment to the long-term restructuring narrative (Feminine Care divestiture, Mexico consolidation, Wet Shave operations consolidation), notwithstanding the ~35% drawdown to ~$22/share at cutoff.
rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for all transactions by named officers and directors during the 24 months preceding cutoff; classify by code (P=open-market purchase, S=open-market sale, M=option exercise, A=award, F=tax-withhold); cross-reference timing with capital events (10-K, 10-Q, divestiture, restructuring announcements).
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (EDGAR ownership.xml direct parse for 55 Form 4 filings) + insider_vs_calendar
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO open-market purchases (code P, $0) by any named officer or director in the entire 24-month window (May 2024 – Feb 2026), across a population including CEO Rod R. Little, CFO Francesca Weissman (appointed Dec 2024), prior CFO/COO Daniel Sullivan, CAO John Dunham, Chief People & Legal Officer LaTanya Langley, President N.A. Jessica Spence, Chief Supply Chain Officer Paul Hibbert, and outside directors Hendra, Hunter, Sachdev, Sit, Stahl, Black, Corbin, Waring, Johnson, O'Leary. Only insider open-market sales were trivial (CAO Dunham 333 sh @ $17.21 = $5,731 on 2025-11-20; one zero-price Hibbert disposition Dec 2024). All other insider activity was option exercise (43 code-M events, 327,791 sh) and tax-withhold surrenders (39 code-F events, 146,432 sh) on RSE/PRSE vests. Critically, the stock declined from ~$34 (May 2024) through ~$32 (Nov 2024) to ~$22 (Feb 2026 buyback prints) over the period — multiple buying windows post-quarterly earnings existed and no insider used them. CEO Little has been CEO since March 2019 and has never been forced into an open-window blackout for an externally-mandated reason; he simply has not bought.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Framework's textbook negative honesty-alpha signal: insiders are NOT lying (disclosure is complete and on time), but they are NOT signaling conviction either. The absence of even a single C-suite or director open-market purchase over a 24-month, ~35%-drawdown window — at a company simultaneously running an aggressive transformation narrative (Feminine Care sale, two restructuring programs, Wet Shave consolidation, $100M new buyback authorization) — is a strong asymmetric negative. The corporate buyback IS executing at ~$22 (Q2 FY26: 674,818 sh for $15M), but personal-capital deployment by C-suite is zero. Distinct from a SEVERE case (no fraud), but the absence-of-buying signal under a 'turnaround' narrative is informative.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K FY2025 (Note on Goodwill): 'At September 30, 2025, after evaluating our sustained decrease in stock price and market capitalization, we concluded that there was a triggering event for our Wet Shave and Skin Care reporting unit requiring an interim impairment analysis ... the fair values of our Wet Shave and Skin Care reporting units exceeded their respective carrying values by 7% and 16%, respectively, and were deemed to be at-risk of future impairment.' Sensitivity table shows a 100bps discount-rate increase reduces Wet Shave fair value by $78.9M (leaving 2.0% cushion); 1.0x market-multiple decrease puts FV $115.4M below carrying (-0.3%). Wet Shave goodwill carrying $1,571M; Banana Boat trade name +4% cushion.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B verification — given Wet Shave was disclosed as 'at-risk' with 7% cushion at Sept 30, 2025, verify whether (a) the cushion has been recomputed in the subsequent two 10-Qs, (b) whether stock decline since the 10-K (filed at ~$28) to cutoff (~$22) constitutes a fresh triggering event, (c) whether management is preemptively disclosing a fresh test.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 FY26 10-Q Note 7 + Q2 FY26 10-Q Note 8, both filed pre-cutoff)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 FY26 10-Q (Feb 9, 2026): 'The Company determined that there were no triggering events requiring an interim impairment analysis during the three months ended December 31, 2025 for its Wet Shave, Sun Care and Skin Care reporting units.' Q2 FY26 10-Q (May 6, 2026): identical language — 'The Company determined that there were no triggering events requiring an interim impairment analysis during the three and six months ended March 31, 2026.' Yet (a) Q1 FY26 net loss from continuing operations was $29.2M on net sales of $422.8M (operating LOSS of $18.9M vs +$9.3M PY); (b) Q2 FY26 Wet Shave segment profit dropped 27.7% Y/Y to $33.7M ($46.6M PY); (c) the Sep 30, 2025 fair value calculation already had cushion of only 7% on $1,571M of goodwill; (d) the stock has declined another ~20% from 10-K filing to cutoff. The 'no triggering event' conclusion in two consecutive quarters becomes increasingly hard to sustain.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the central Mode-B catch. EPC explicitly disclosed Wet Shave goodwill was 'at-risk' with sensitivity tables showing the cushion vanishes on any modestly adverse assumption shift, then concluded in two subsequent 10-Qs that no triggering event existed despite (a) reporting an operating LOSS in Q1, (b) the stock declining another ~20%, (c) Wet Shave segment profit -28% Y/Y in Q2. The Sun and Skin Care segment is also relevant: Banana Boat trade name had 4% cushion. Goodwill at risk: $1,571M (Wet Shave) + $432M (Skin Care, 16% cushion) + ~$277M (Banana Boat). A material Wet Shave impairment in Q3/Q4 FY26 is a near-mechanical consequence of the carrying-value math the company itself disclosed. Severity SEVERE because the issuer's own sensitivity disclosure shows a 100bps discount-rate increase removes the cushion entirely, yet management has avoided the triggering-event conclusion.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K and Q1 FY26 10-Q: 'On November 6, 2025, the Board of Directors approved the Company entering into an asset purchase agreement to sell its Feminine Care reportable segment for $340.0, subject to a purchase price adjustment upon closing... The divestiture of the Feminine Care segment is a key step to transform Edgewell into a more focused, agile and consumer-driven personal care company.' (Closed Feb 2, 2026 for $340M to Essity.)
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A verification (existence/economics) + Mode B (what was the actual P&L of the divested segment, the impairment recorded, and the realized use of proceeds vs the narrative).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 21, Q1 FY26 Note 2 — Discontinued Operations, Q2 FY26 Note 2)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mode A passes: definitive agreement Nov 12, 2025 with Essity AB; closed Feb 2, 2026; cash-free debt-free proceeds $340M; reclassified as discontinued operations and assets held-for-sale. Mode B: (a) GOODWILL IMPAIRMENT of $37.4M on the Feminine Care disposal group in Q1 FY26 was REQUIRED at hold-for-sale classification (offer price $340M < carrying), incremental to the $51.1M Q4 FY25 impairment already recorded on the same segment — total $88.5M of impairment on a segment sold for $340M; (b) Q2 FY26 final loss-on-sale adjustment: additional $2.2M; (c) discontinued-operations losses: $(51.1)M for six months ended Mar 31, 2026 vs $16.2M earnings PY (the segment was profitable); (d) Feminine Care FY2025 segment profit was $15.6M (down 45.8% from $28.8M PY) — i.e., the divested business had been declining sharply; (e) USE OF PROCEEDS: full $140M revolver paydown (good), $55M cash taxes (~16% of proceeds), $15.8M H1 buybacks, $14.5M dividends — net cash position grew to $299.7M from $225.7M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is complete and the cash trade is positive (revolver paydown, net debt reduced ~$220M). But the narrative-quality issue is that EPC presented the divestiture as a strategic 'transformation' step when (a) Feminine Care had been showing accelerating decline, (b) the company took $88.5M of cumulative goodwill impairment to get to the sale price, (c) the discontinued-operations loss in Q1 alone ($36.5M) exceeded H1 buyback ($15.8M). The 'transformation' framing obscures that this was largely an underperforming asset sold at a price requiring a write-down. Moderate not severe because the price ($340M) is real cash and the use of proceeds is rational.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'In fiscal 2025, we recorded pre-tax restructuring and related costs of $53.1, consisting largely of severance, project implementation and other exit costs in support of cost efficiency programs ... we expect to incur pre-tax charges of approximately $49.0 in fiscal 2026.' Q2 FY26 10-Q: 'In fiscal 2026, the Company announced a plan to further consolidate its North America Wet Shave operations ... the Company is anticipating incurring restructuring and related charges of $27 in fiscal 2026 and the consolidation is expected to be completed by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2028.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify the cumulative restructuring drumbeat against the issuer's framing of these as transient 'support of cost efficiency programs', and check H1 FY26 actual run-rate against the $49M+$27M = $76M FY26 plan.
rfm_tuples.M_value: H1 FY26 restructuring charges already total $47.4M ($32.1M of which hit P&L as restructuring, $0.8M in SG&A, $12.6M in COGS, $0.2M in discontinued operations, plus $1.8M COGS in the new Wet Shave plan). Run-rate suggests FY26 will materially exceed the original $49M Mexico-consolidation plan; the new Wet Shave program adds another $27M; with two more quarters remaining, total FY26 likely $80M+ vs $53M FY25 vs $36M FY24. This is the FIFTH consecutive year of 'one-time' restructuring (FY22-FY26). Cumulative restructuring 2022-2026: well in excess of $200M. The 'adjusted EPS' metric on which management is compensated systematically excludes this — adjusted FY25 EPS $2.52 vs GAAP $0.53.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: restructuring is functionally a recurring operating cost dressed as non-GAAP add-back. Five-year cumulative pattern undermines the 'adjusted' framing. Not severe because each individual program is disclosed and the cash effect is clearly stated — but the cumulative honesty-test on adjusted-EPS framing fails. Important context for valuing the franchise: 'true' earnings power closer to GAAP than adjusted.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Executive Summary FY2025: 'Net sales for fiscal 2025 decreased $30.2, or 1.3%, to $2,223.5, including a $0.2 unfavorable impact due to currency movements. Organic net sales decreased $30.0, or 1.3% ... Net earnings for fiscal 2025 decreased $73.2, or 74.2%, to $25.4.' Continuing-operations restated post-Feminine-Care divestiture.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check FY25 GAAP trajectory against H1 FY26 continuing operations to test whether the rate of decline accelerated and whether organic growth is materializing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 + Q2 FY26 condensed consolidated income statements, continuing ops basis)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Continuing operations basis (post Feminine Care discop): Q1 FY26 net sales $422.8M (+1.9% Y/Y) but operating LOSS of $18.9M vs operating income of $9.3M PY; net loss from continuing ops $(29.2)M vs $(10.1)M PY. Q2 FY26 net sales $519.5M (+0.6% Y/Y) but ORGANIC NET SALES DECREASED $12.6M, or 2.4%; operating income $18.4M vs $49.0M PY; net income from continuing ops $4.0M vs $20.8M PY. Six-month FY26 net sales $942.3M (+1.1% Y/Y reported; organic down); operating LOSS $(0.5)M vs $58.3M PY; net loss from continuing ops $(25.2)M vs $10.7M PY. North America volume continues to decline (Q2 -4.8% organic) and is now offset only by international (+1.0%). Wet Shave segment profit H1: $75.9M vs $93.2M PY (-18.6%); Sun and Skin Care H1: $44.0M vs $47.4M PY. Both core segments contracting.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Operating performance has demonstrably worsened post-10-K. The 10-K's framing ('international markets delivered organic growth of 3.5%') is technically accurate but mathematically does not offset N.A. decline. The shift from operating income $58.3M to operating LOSS $(0.5)M H1 Y/Y on continuing ops is the structural read. Not severe because the disclosure is complete; moderate because the 10-K's tone of resilience is at odds with the realized H1 FY26 P&L.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Liquidity section: '$1.4 billion ... Approximately $1.3 billion (90%) of our debt balance as of September 30, 2025, is borrowed at fixed interest rates ranging from 4.125% to 5.50% with maturity dates in 2028 and thereafter ... We also have $750.0 million of senior notes, fixed interest rate of 5.5%, due 2028 and $500.0 million of senior notes, fixed interest rate of 4.1%, due 2029.' Revolver matures 2029 with springing-maturity triggers (March 2, 2028 if 2028 notes >$150M outstanding; Dec 29, 2028 if 2029 notes >$150M outstanding).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given a $750M 2028 maturity and a $500M 2029 maturity, evaluate the refinancing risk at current credit conditions and operating trajectory, and the embedded covenant pressure (debt/EBITDA <= 4.0x, interest coverage >= 3.0x).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 12 Debt + Q2 FY26 Note 11 Debt) + computed leverage from FY25 financials
rfm_tuples.M_value: Capital structure at Q2 FY26: long-term notes $1,250M fixed; short-term notes $35M; revolver $0 (paid down with divestiture proceeds, $418.8M available); total borrowings $1,285M; cash $299.7M; net debt ~$985M. FY25 EBITDA (back-solved): operating income $96.6M + D&A from cash flow ~$76M (per FY25 footnotes) = ~$172M GAAP; adjusted ~$280M. Net leverage ~3.5x adjusted / ~5.7x GAAP. Springing revolver maturity to Mar 2, 2028 unless the company refinances the $750M 5.5% 2028 notes down to <$150M outstanding before then. Refinancing window critical 2026-2027. Coupon math: 5.5% notes refinanced today at current single-B comps would likely be 7-8%+ (i.e., +$15-20M annual interest on $750M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K language ('Approximately $1.3 billion (90%) of our debt ... fixed interest rates ranging from 4.125% to 5.50%') frames the fixed-rate as protective but understates the refinancing problem. The 2028 wall is $750M of 5.5% paper that needs to be repriced into a deteriorated operating environment and likely higher credit spread, plus a springing covenant in the revolver that forces action before Mar 2028. Net debt is manageable today (-$220M post-divestiture), but the FY26 operating trajectory raises real questions about whether EBITDA supports a refi at par. Not severe yet because the 2028 maturity is still 2+ years out; moderate because management did not stress-test this in the MD&A.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Goodwill and Intangibles Note: 'The fair values of our Bulldog and Banana Boat trade names exceeded their respective carrying values by 9% and 4%, respectively, and were deemed to be at-risk of future impairment.' Banana Boat carrying $277.2M.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given that Banana Boat (the major sun-care brand) had only 4% cushion at July 1, 2025, and the Sun & Skin Care segment H1 FY26 profitability has decelerated (segment profit $44.0M vs $47.4M PY, -7.2%), verify whether a subsequent impairment risk is properly flagged.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Neither Q1 nor Q2 FY26 10-Q identifies a triggering event for indefinite-lived intangibles (Banana Boat $277M, Bulldog $10M). Same 'no triggering event' boilerplate. Q2 FY26 segment profit for Sun and Skin Care was actually $47.6M (+slightly Q-o-Q) but H1 segment profit declined 7.2% Y/Y due to weaker Q1; the segment is meaningfully exposed to (a) sun-care seasonality, (b) tariffs/IEEPA — Hawaiian Tropic and Banana Boat have China-sourced inputs, (c) Sun Care 'reformulation costs' charged as adjustments ($2.7M H1) implying continued product-quality / regulatory pressure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 4% cushion on Banana Boat is small enough that even a modest reformulation-cost increase or a multiple compression on comparable beauty/sun-care peers triggers impairment. Not severe because the segment is currently profitable; moderate because the at-risk disclosure was made in the 10-K but has not been re-disclosed or re-tested in subsequent 10-Qs.

rfm_tuples.R: Q2 FY26 10-Q Other Matters: 'On February 20, 2026 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) by the executive branch are not lawful ... On March 4, 2026, the Court of International Trade (CIT) issued an additional ruling that importers that paid tariffs under IEEPA are due refunds ... As of March 31, 2026, the Company has not recognized an asset related to the potential refund of IEEPA tariffs paid. The ultimate availability, timing and amount of any potential refunds of such tariffs is highly uncertain.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — does the registry of US Supreme Court rulings and Court of International Trade orders confirm the dates and the refund eligibility? Mode B — quantify the order of magnitude of the potential refund asset given EPC's stated reliance on Mexico and China sourcing.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q2 FY26 Other Matters) + 10-K Item 1A Risk Factor on tariffs (lines 449-452)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mode A passes — both rulings (Feb 20, 2026 SCOTUS + Mar 4, 2026 CIT) are court-of-record events; EPC's disclosure of dates is consistent. Mode B: this is an UPSIDE Mode-B implied finding rather than a downside. EPC explicitly identifies Mexico and China as primary import sources (10-K p. 12, '[we] rely on materials, components and finished goods that are sourced from or manufactured in foreign countries, including Mexico and China'). FY25 cost of goods sold was $1,298.6M (= 41.6% margin on $2,223.5M sales). If IEEPA tariff incidence on EPC imports averaged even 1-3% of COGS over the affected period (2025-2026), the refund magnitude could be $20-60M+. Company correctly applies ASC 450 — gain contingency not yet probable/estimable — and refuses to record an asset (conservative).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Conservative accounting treatment is appropriate per ASC 450. The disclosure is honest, the legal basis is real, and there is a real-money upside option that is currently valued at zero on the balance sheet. This is offsetting (positive) information vs the rest of the picture. Not material enough to change the overall composite but worth noting as a non-zero option.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 5: 'On November 13, 2025, the Board approved an authorization to repurchase for up to $100.0, superseding the previous share repurchase authorization from January 2018' (which had been 10.0 million shares).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify whether the reset/reduction in buyback authorization (from a multi-year ~10M share authority to $100M dollar-capped) is consistent with management's stated capital-allocation discipline, given that the company is simultaneously buying at depressed prices.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K + Q2 FY26 Item 2 issuer purchases table)
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY25 buyback was $90.2M (2.8M shares) at average prices likely in the $30s (stock peaked ~$35 in early 2025). H1 FY26 buyback only $15.8M (0.7M shares) at $22.22-$22.31 in Feb-Mar 2026 — i.e., buying meaningfully into weakness but at <20% of FY25 pace. The Nov 2025 authorization reset replaced an open share-count authorization (which had ~6.6M shares remaining at FY25 ~$25 = ~$165M of capacity) with a SMALLER dollar-cap ($100M). Net: the corporate buyback machinery was constrained at the very moment when the stock was cheapest. Possible structural reasons: (a) need to preserve cash for $750M 2028 refi; (b) operating cash flow $118.4M FY25 doesn't comfortably support both restructuring spend ($53M+$49M+$27M) AND material buybacks AND dividends ($29M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: the buyback authorization reset narrative ('routine governance refresh') obscures the practical effect of constraining capital return at the cyclical low. Combined with the zero insider purchases, this paints a picture of corporate capital that knows the cash needs to be conserved for the 2028 maturity, even though the public framing remains 'opportunistic.' Moderate because the math is fully disclosed in the buyback table; the framing is the issue.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 3 Legal Proceedings: 'We, and our subsidiaries, are subject to a number of legal proceedings in various jurisdictions arising out of our operations during the ordinary course of business ... The amount of liability, if any, from these proceedings cannot be determined with certainty. If one or more legal matters were resolved against us, the Company's financial condition and operating results could be materially adversely affected.' (No specific cases or amounts named.) Q2 FY26 10-Q reveals a $4.7M settlement charge for a former contract manufacturing dispute.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — given the 10-K's blanket boilerplate, verify what specific legal exposures are visible in the subsequent 10-Qs.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 + Q2 FY26 10-Q Note on Commitments and Contingencies; Q2 FY26 Other Matters)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q2 FY26 10-Q discloses $4.7M settlement of 'certain claims and disputes in connection with a former contract manufacturing agreement' — a NEW specific matter not flagged in the 10-K's Item 3. Also referenced as a non-GAAP 'Legal matter' adjustment in the EPS reconciliation. No other named matters disclosed in either 10-Q. The amount is immaterial ($4.7M pre-tax) but the disclosure pattern (named only after settlement) is a Mode-B indicator that the 10-K's Item 3 is functionally uninformative.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Cannot confirm or refute the existence of larger undisclosed contingencies. The disclosed $4.7M is immaterial. The framework grades the 10-K's Item 3 as content-free boilerplate but cannot independently verify whether material contingencies are being withheld. Net: UNVERIFIABLE, not a material driver of the composite.

summary: EPC is a Mode-B-rich case where the dominant signal is the Wet Shave goodwill at-risk disclosure ($1,571M carrying, only 7% cushion at Sep 30, 2025, sensitivity tables that put the cushion at -0.3% on a 1.0x multiple compression) combined with management's 'no triggering event' conclusion in BOTH subsequent 10-Qs despite a 20% additional stock decline and Wet Shave segment profit -19% YoY H1 FY26. Form 4 evidence is the second pillar: ZERO open-market purchases by ANY of 18+ named officers and directors across the entire 24-month window through the ~35% drawdown — a textbook absence-of-conviction signal. Feminine Care divestiture is positive cash trade but required cumulative $90.7M of impairments; H1 FY26 continuing ops is at operating LOSS vs +$58M PY; restructuring charges are now structurally recurring ($76M planned FY26, the fifth consecutive year). Offsets: IEEPA tariff refund is a real (unquantified) upside option; balance sheet is fine NEAR-term (net debt $985M, no revolver draw, $300M cash) but $750M 2028 maturity at 5.5% needs refi in a deteriorating operating environment. VERDICT: SHORT-tier — the goodwill impairment IS coming (mathematically near-mechanical given disclosed sensitivities), management is delaying recognition, insiders are signaling no conviction with personal capital, and the 2028 refi wall is closer than the issuer's framing implies.
